summary.text: A lever is a rigid beam that turns about a fixed point called the fulcrum, and it is one of the six classic simple machines.
In an ideal lever the ratio of output force to input force equals the ratio of the distances from the fulcrum to where each force acts.
Levers come in three classes depending on whether the fulcrum, the load or the effort sits in the middle, from seesaws to wheelbarrows to fishing rods.

facts.label: Mechanical advantage
facts.value: Output force divided by input force

items.prompt: You lift a loaded wheelbarrow by its handles, and it feels much lighter than the load. Why?

options.label: Your hands are nearer the pivot than the load
The wheel stores energy and gives it back
The load sits closer to the wheel's pivot than your hands do
The lever adds energy to your effort

items.explain: The load arm is shorter than the effort arm, so the mechanical advantage is above one.

items.prompt: You squeeze tweezers hard, but the tips pinch with less force than your fingers apply. What explains that?

options.label: Your fingers sit nearer the pivot than the tips do
Tweezers have no fulcrum to use
The fulcrum is between fingers and tips
They are compound levers that divide force

items.explain: With the effort between load and fulcrum, the effort arm is shorter, so the mechanical advantage is below one.

items.prompt: An adult twice a child's weight sits on a seesaw. Where must the child sit to balance?

options.label: The same distance from the pivot
Half as far from the pivot
Right next to the pivot
Twice as far from the pivot

items.explain: Balance of moments about the fulcrum means force ratio is the inverse of the distance ratio.

items.prompt: Using a long crowbar, you lift a heavy stone with an easy push. What do you give up?

options.label: Some of the stone's weight
Nothing at all
Distance, since your end moves farther
The stone's stored energy

items.explain: A lever trades force against movement, so a small input force goes with a longer input travel.

items.prompt: A seesaw, a pair of scissors and a crowbar share which layout?

options.label: The load sits between effort and pivot
The effort sits between load and pivot
The pivot sits between effort and load
There is no pivot at all

items.explain: These are class I levers, with the fulcrum between the effort and the resistance.

items.prompt: In a nail clipper, the output of one lever becomes the push on the next. What is that arrangement called?

options.label: A compound lever
A lever with a mechanical advantage of one
A lever without a fulcrum
A speed multiplier lever

items.explain: Several levers acting in series, with each load serving as the next effort, make a compound lever.
